why_how.text: Anyone who lives in West Virginia and wants to drive a motor vehicle on public roads must hold a West Virginia driver's license unless expressly exempt, and must carry that license while driving.
A person operating a motor vehicle in the armed services of the United States while performing official duties is exempt from the West Virginia license requirement.
A nonresident who is at least sixteen years old and holds a valid license from another state or country is exempt from needing a West Virginia license, but only for ninety days in a calendar year.
A nonresident attending a West Virginia college or university who holds a valid license from another state is exempt from the West Virginia license requirement.
A habitual user of alcoholic beverages or a person addicted to narcotic drugs can be denied a driver's license.
A person whose driver's license has been suspended or revoked by West Virginia, another state or a foreign jurisdiction can be denied a license until that suspension or revocation period expires.
A license can be denied to anyone the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe would endanger public safety or welfare when operating a motor vehicle.
A person under the age of eighteen who is neither enrolled in nor graduated from an approved educational institution can be denied a driver's license.

The ninety-day calendar-year limit attaches to the general exemption for nonresident drivers at least sixteen years old with a valid out-of-state license, not to the separate exemption for nonresident college students.

why_how.text: An immigrant applying for a permit, license or identification card provides a Social Security number, two proofs of West Virginia residency, and one of a Permanent Resident Card, a valid temporary resident stamp in a foreign passport with English translation or on the arrival record, or a valid re-entry permit.

A non-immigrant applicant provides a Social Security number or a Social Security Administration denial letter, two residency proofs, a valid foreign passport, the federal arrival record, a visa when the applicant's nation requires one, original documents verifying status and authorized stay, and written school verification for student statuses or employer verification for work statuses.

A refugee applicant provides a Social Security number or denial letter, two residency proofs, an arrival record showing the grant of refugee status, a Reception and Placement Program Assurance form, and written verification of identity and residency from an employee of a State Department approved sponsoring organization.

A refugee without an approved sponsoring organization, or a person seeking asylum, provides two residency proofs, a Social Security number or denial letter, an arrival record stamped as refugee or asylee, and employment authorization documents.

Non-immigrant and refugee applicants may substitute a Social Security Administration denial letter for a Social Security number, while the immigrant document list on the same page names only the Social Security number.
